statement_record.book: A category has all finite limits iff it has all finite products and all equalizers (equivalently: iff it has pullbacks and a terminal object). Proof by construction: for D : J → C finite, take P0 = ∏_{i∈J0} D_i and P1 = ∏_{(α:i→j)∈J1} D_j, define φ, ψ : P0 → P1 by π_α∘φ = π_{cod α} and π_α∘ψ = D_α∘π_{dom α}, and let e : E → P0 be their equalizer; then (E, π_i∘e) is the limit of D.
statement_record.intree: Only the converse, shape-by-shape: `Cartesian_Limit : (∀ F : Two_Discrete ⟶ C, Limit F) ↔ @Cartesian C`; `Terminal_Limit (F : 0 ⟶ C) : Limit F ↔ @Terminal C`; `Complete_HasEqualizers : @Complete A → HasEqualizers A`. Structure/Equalizer.v and Structure/Pullback.v cite the existence theorem in prose (the latter as an open `jww` TODO) without proving it.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: only the trivial direction (a category with limits of a given shape has the corresponding structure) is proved, and even that is done one shape at a time and with the equalizer half derived from FULL completeness (`@Complete A`) rather than from finite limits. The substantive direction — the equalizer-of-two-products construction that manufactures an arbitrary (finite) limit — is nowhere in the tree, and there is no in-tree notion of a finite diagram or of `has all finite limits` at all (`Complete` quantifies over all diagram categories, size being carried implicitly by universe polymorphism).

Definition PreservesImageLimit : Type := ∀ (J : Category) (G : J ⟶ C) (L : Limit G) (N : Cone (U ◯ G)), ∃! φ : vertex_obj[N] ~{D}~> U L, ∀ x : J, image_leg L x ∘ φ ≈ cone_leg N x.  (* image_leg L x := fmap[U] (limit_leg (limit_is_alimit L) x) *)

"The bare class [PreservesLimit] of [Structure/Limit/Preservation.v] records only that the *apex object* [U L] carries *some* limit structure of [U ◯ G] ([IsALimit (U ◯ G) (U L)]); the legs of that structure are left unconstrained and need not be the image legs [fmap[U] π_•]. statement_record.book: F : C → D preserves limits of type J when for every diagram D : J → C and every limiting cone p_j : L → D_j the IMAGE cone F p_j : F L → F D_j is a limiting cone for F∘D; briefly F(lim D_j) ≅ lim F(D_j) via the canonical comparison. A functor preserving all limits is called continuous.
statement_record.intree: Two inequivalent notions coexist. Apex-only, per-diagram: `Class PreservesLimit G F := { preserves_limit (L : Limit G) : IsALimit (F ◯ G) (F L) }`, with `PreservesAllLimits F := ∀ J G, PreservesLimit G F` as `continuous`. Cone-level, all-shapes, section-bound to one functor U : `PreservesImageLimit := ∀ J G (L : Limit G) (N : Cone (U ◯ G)), ∃! φ, ∀ x, fmap[U] (limit_leg L x) ∘ φ ≈ cone_leg N x`.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker for the named class: `PreservesLimit`/`PreservesAllLimits` assert only that the apex object F L admits SOME limit structure for F ◯ G, not that the image cone (F applied to the limit legs) is limiting — the library itself proves this insufficient in the Construction/Comma/Limit.v header and refuses to use the class for GAFT/SAFT. The faithful cone-level rendering of `continuous` exists as `PreservesImageLimit`, but only in the all-shapes bundled form.

Definition IsAColimit `(F : J ⟶ C) (c : C) : Type := IsALimit (F^op) c.  Definition cocone_inj `{F : J ⟶ C} (N : Cocone F) (x : J) : F x ~{C}~> vertex_obj[N].  Lemma cocone_inj_coherence (N : Cocone F) {x y} (f : x ~> y) : cocone_inj N y ∘ fmap[F] f ≈ cocone_inj N x.  Definition ump_colimit `(H : @IsAColimit J C F c) (N : Cocone F) : ∃! u : c ~{C}~> vertex_obj[N], ∀ x : J, u ∘ colimit_inj H x ≈ cocone_inj N x.

statement_record.book: Dual to Def 5.18, in running prose. A cocone from the base D : J → C is an object C (vertex) with arrows c_j : D_j → C such that c_j ∘ D(α) = c_i for every α : i → j. A morphism of cocones f : (C,(c_j)) → (C',(c'_j)) is f : C → C' with f ∘ c_j = c'_j for all j. A colimit for D is an initial object in the category of cocones — a cocone mapping uniquely to any other cocone from D; written colim_{j∈J} D_j.
statement_record.intree: `Cocone F := Cone (F^op)` (apex plus legs `cocone_inj N x : F x ~> vertex_obj[N]` with coherence `cocone_inj N y ∘ fmap[F] f ≈ cocone_inj N x` — exactly the book's c_j ∘ D(α) = c_i); `Cocones F := Cones (F^op)`, whose morphisms are apex maps `u` with `vertex_map[L] ∘ u ≈ vertex_map[N]` read in C^op, i.e. `u ∘ c_j ≈ c'_j`, identified when their underlying apex maps agree (the commutativity witness is proof-irrelevant); `Colimit F := Limit (F^op)`, with `ump_colimit : ∃! u : c ~> N, ∀ x, u ∘ colimit_inj H x ≈ cocone_inj N x`.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same, with the dual formulated definitionally rather than restated (the library's duality architecture makes C^op^op = C hold by reflexivity, so the cocone/colimit notions are the cone/limit notions transported, and covariant accessors `cocone_inj`, `colimit_inj`, `ump_colimit`, `colimit_med`, `colimit_med_unique` re-expose everything in C). One presentational difference: `Colimit F` is defined as the universal cocone (terminal object of `Cones (F^op)`) rather than literally as `Initial (Cocones F)`; the two are the same statement — `Cocones F := Cones (F^op)` and initial-in-C-cocones is terminal-in-C^op-cones — and Instance/Cones/Limit.v:37 supplies the round trip `Limit_Cones : Terminal (Cones F) → Limit F`, which dualizes. Setoid rephrasing (≈ for =) is the library's faithful convention.
